implementation_notes: The typed object parameter is the TypeScript realization: declare the shape as an `interface` or `type` alias with optional (`?`) properties, take one parameter of that type and destructure it with defaults in the signature; `readonly` plus `Partial`/`Pick`/`Omit` derive variants of the shape, and the compiler rejects wrong property types and missing required properties. A class is only worth it when the carrier needs runtime behaviour or validation, and across a wire boundary the type is erased, so the data must be validated instead of trusted.
pitfalls: Types are erased at runtime: JSON from an API can violate `DrawParams` while the compiler stays happy - validate at the boundary.
Excess-property checking only fires for fresh object literals; assigning through a variable lets unrelated properties travel along unnoticed.
Destructuring discards the object, so a function that forwards the carrier must take the parameter itself (`function f(params: DrawParams)`).
